away.blurb: There’s obviously an extra motivating factor for Skattebo to be ready for Sunday’s game against Philadelphia because last year’s ankle injury happened on the Lincoln Financial Field turf, and for him to return to the scene of the crime and post another career day that matches or tops his Houston performance (17 carries, 124 yards, one touchdown) would bring his comeback full circle. If Skattebo isn’t at least limited in the next day or two, it might make sense for him to sit out Sunday’s game so he’s ready for the clash against the Commanders on Thursday night. NFL Week 7 Winners and Losers: Seahawks Spoil Kenneth Walker III’s Return to Seattle Giants RB Cam Skattebo Misses Practice With Hamstring Injury Ahead of Eagles Game Skip to main content SI.COM New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (hamstring) tops the team’s Week 9 injury report after missing Wednesday’s practice. Skattebo was injured on his 42-yard run in overtime against the Houston Texans two weeks ago. At the time, he tried to downplay the injury, but head coach John Harbaugh later characterized the running back as “day to day up to the game,” and said, “We’re just going to have to see where we’re at.” Where things stand doesn’t look very promising, as hamstrings are tricky injuries and Skattebo’s absence from practice has raised concerns for the Giants, especially since Tyrone Tracy Jr. is currently on injured reserve with his own hamstring injury, also suffered in the game against the Texans. Skattebo undoubtedly doesn’t want to miss any more time, especially after losing most of his rookie campaign last year to an ankle injury. If Skattebo can’t go, the Giants will likely turn to Devin Singletary as their lead back. They also have Greg Desrosiers on the roster, whom they signed off the Los Angeles Chargers practice squad last week, and they will likely elevate either Phil Mafaha or Eric Gray, the latter signed this week to the practice squad, for Sunday’s game. "I feel very confident about the running back situation. I like the guys we've got," Harbaugh said. "Obviously, Motor (Devin Singletary) has been here. We've got some guys that have been here in the past, too, that we brought in, as you know, that were here, and we also brought in one, (running back) Eric (Gray). "So, I feel good about it. We claimed a guy off the Chargers (Gregory Desrosiers). He's a very talented, young guy. So, those guys are in practice. They've got two practices now, and if they have to go, they'll definitely be ready to roll." While it’s too soon to say for certain what Skattebo’s status will be for Sunday, keep in mind that the Giants have a short work week following their game against Philadelphia. Sitting Sunday would give him a few extra days to get right for that game, and a longer break afterward to make more progress on his hamstring. Hurts was ruled out for the remainder of the season after having been found to have multiple blood clots in his lungs last month, throwing his career into doubt. But top NFL officials have hit out at the 'nonsense' around Hurts' injury, claiming 'considerable and uninformed speculation' was spread about the case. Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts made an appearance at the team's facilities on Wednesday following his recent health scare. Weeks on from the horrific ordeal, the Super Bowl winner reunited with his teammates, some of whom hadn't seen him since he was placed on injured reserve, on Wednesday. Hurts is said to have sat in on the team meetings and additional meetings but did not address the team, according to ESPN's Tim McManus. Head coach Nick Sirianni did not address Hurts' attendance when questioned by reporters on Wednesday but did stress how much he misses his quarterback. I know he's resting and recovering, and we're all still praying for him and hoping for a speedy recovery.' Hurts was placed on injured reserve on October 17 following the Eagles' game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London in Week 5. Kyren Williams’ one-yard touchdown gave Los Angeles a 10-9 halftime lead. Blake Corum then broke off a 23-yard touchdown run and Matthew Stafford hit Puka Nacua for an 18-yard score in the third quarter. Stafford finished 17-of-25 for 157 yards, one touchdown and one interception, Nacua caught 11 passes for 80 yards and a score, and the Rams rushed for 129 yards while their defense intercepted Justin Herbert twice and kept the Chargers out of the end zone. The Commanders are coming off a much-needed 27-10 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles, their first win in more than a month. Washington fell behind 10-0 during a penalty-filled first quarter before scoring the game’s final 27 points and shutting Philadelphia out over the final three quarters. Jayden Daniels completed 16 of 29 passes for 217 yards, a touchdown and no interceptions, connecting with Stefon Diggs for an eight-yard score, while Rachaad White ran 11 times for 55 yards and the clinching touchdown. Washington finished with 135 yards rushing, but its defense was the bigger story, sacking Tanner McKee five times, intercepting him once and limiting Saquon Barkley to just 30 yards on 13 carries. That showing by the Washington defense sets up the primary storyline for Sunday’s game: the Commanders’ resurgent pass rush against Stafford. The other of course relates to Daniels and his ability to attack a banged-up Rams’ secondary. Historically, Washington has had the upper hand in the series, holding a 24-13-1 regular season record against the Rams, but recent meetings have been much more balanced. Washington has split its past four matchups with Los Angeles dating to 2015, and Sunday’s game will be the Rams’ first trip to Washington since 2020, when Los Angeles won 30-10 in the game that marked Alex Smith’s remarkable return to action following multiple leg surgeries and a long rehab. Rams coach Sean McVay spent seven seasons in Washington’s organization and three as its offensive coordinator before taking the Rams’ job. away.headline: Fair to wonder if the players… feel the same way — Rams analyst weighs in on Matthew Stafford’s wife Kelly raising issue with NFL’s schedule
away.blurb: “Given that Kelly Stafford spoke out about the Rams’ lack of a true bye week, it’s fair to wonder if the players, especially Matthew Stafford, feel the same way,” Grisak continued. “With the number of injuries that the Rams have had to manage this season, the extra four days would likely have been beneficial.” Jaylen Watson (shoulder), Poona Ford (triceps) and Blake Grupe (ACL) have all been ruled out for the season. Meanwhile, Trent McDuffie (back), Kam Curl (foot) and Colby Parkinson (ribs) have also missed practice with injury concerns. The Los Angeles Rams are facing an unusual scheduling challenge this season, and Matthew Stafford’s wife, Kelly, isn’t happy about it. The NFL introduced its first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game this season, with the Rams scheduled to face the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday, November 25. As a result, Los Angeles will have just 10 days between its Week 10 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals on November 15 and its game against Green Bay. While both teams will follow the same schedule, the shortened break has raised questions about player recovery, particularly for the Rams, who have already dealt with several injuries this season. Blaine Grisak Responds to Kelly Stafford’s Scheduling Complaint The controversy started when Kelly Stafford took to Instagram to question why the Rams were the only team without a proper bye week. “Just curious to hear the thought process behind making the Rams the only team in the NFL without a true bye week. Because d***, after 18 years around this league, even I need a week off during the season and I have never played a single snap. I’m tired just watching from the stands. Can’t imagine how the guys feel,” she wrote. Kelly’s comments highlighted the challenges of getting through a 17-game NFL season. Even those watching from the sidelines can feel the demands of the schedule, making it difficult to imagine what players go through while dealing with injuries and physical exhaustion. Rams analyst Blaine Grisak acknowledged Kelly’s concerns, noting that the Rams are not the only team affected. “There is certainly reason for criticism for how the NFL came up with the Rams’ schedule. The lack of a true bye week is one of them. With that said, the Packers will be in the same situation,” Grisak wrote via Sports Illustrated. However, he made it clear that having another team face the same problem does not make the schedule fair. “That doesn’t mean that the NFL shouldn’t be criticized,” he added. “Teams are given one bye week per season and the NFL has taken that away from two teams. With the NFL scheduling games on Thanksgiving Eve, it wouldn’t be surprising if two more teams faced the same situation next year.” Rams’ Injury Problems Make the Shortened Break More Concerning The scheduling issue becomes even more concerning when considering the number of injuries the Rams, who rank 11th on PFN’s Offense Impact Metric , have dealt with this season. away.headline: Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett Returns, But Bad News Continues to Pile Up
away.blurb: While the Los Angeles Rams got some good injury news on Wednesday, the injuries also continue to pile up. Both Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson opened their practice windows as they work to return from injured reserve. However, cornerback Jaylen Watson’s season is over with a shoulder injury and cornerback Trent McDuffie was a non-participant with a back injury. The biggest knock for the Rams is Watson being placed on injured reserve and being out for the season. Watson was the team’s top free agent signing as the Rams looked to rebuild their cornerback room this offseason. After missing Week 4 with a dislocated shoulder, Watson reaggravated the injury in the third quarter of the team’s win against the Chargers. “The likelihood of it coming out and doing further damage to it is a very high probability. You could strap it, but it would restrict his movement,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Just some of the different things that we've received from our doctors, it's the right thing to do by him, even though it sucks because he's been such a bright spot for us.” “It's exciting. It's great to be able to get him back out there,” said McVay. “He'll probably take half the reps today. If you have 30 reps, he'll take 15 and then we'll see how he feels coming out of that. Hopefully, it's just a little bit of an increase incrementally at a time.” In addition to Garrett being back, Ferguson and running back Ronnie Rivers returned to practice as well. Ferguson should provide some insurance if Parkinson can’t play for a second straight week, while Rivers could be helpful on special teams. Also limited were linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), left guard Steve Avila (hamstring), and wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back). Coming out of the Chargers game, one of the big stories was Matthew Stafford being seen walking out of the locker room with ice around his right arm . Stafford showed up as a full participant on Wednesday’s injury report with a right elbow injury. home.blurb: Javon Kinlaw missed practice all week, so it wasn't much of a surprise when the Washington Commanders officially listed him as out on their final injury report Friday. The surprise was Daron Payne , who was added with a foot injury; he's officially questionable after being limited in practice on the last day. John Bates, Treylon Burks, and Jer’Zhan Newton were all also listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against Philadelphia. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window as he returns from a pectoral injury ; the Commanders must still activate him before he's eligible. Bates improved from not practicing at all to limited, while Burks went from limited to not practicing , then back to limited on Friday . Commanders head coach Dan Quinn didn't hide how impressed he was with Newton's recovery work Wednesday: "Man, he has worked his ass off." Luke McCaffrey, Charles Omenihu , and Deatrich Wise Jr. were limited Friday but carried no game designation; Omenihu was limited all week with groin/ankle injuries. Nick Allegretti rebounded from missing Thursday's practice by returning as a full participant Friday. picks.headline: 3 bold predictions for Panthers in season-defining matchup with Broncos
picks.blurb: The Carolina Panthers have fallen to 3-4 after a really inspiring 3-2 start. Losing two games in a row in a demoralizing fashion, at least on the offensive side of the ball, is crushing, but it's especially bad when the schedule has no reprieve. The Panthers have to turn it around. Unfortunately, they've got the AFC West-leading Denver Broncos coming to town. The Panthers are underdogs , and no one's picking them to win. It could be another ugly one. But in the spirit of success, here are some bold predictions for the contest. Bryce Young is sacked less than twice Being sacked twice in a game doesn't feel like a bold prediction. But Bryce Young has been sacked 11 times in the last two games. Getting back down to a normal number of sacks feels like an impossible task for everyone involved, especially the offensive line that can't seem to hold up for even two seconds. The offensive line could look different (and should). Young's knee should be healthier, so he can get back to evading pressure as he did in the early going. And Brad Idzik should have enough data to call plays to help offset the porous line. Young's health, a better line, and smarter planning should help the sacks and pressure regress to the mean. Bo Nix passes for less than 200 yards You'd be forgiven for checking the Panthers' depth chart and not knowing who the cornerbacks were. For an offense (Denver's) that has struggled to throw the ball down the field, Carolina's secondary has to feel like a gift from above. But Marco Wilson was solid in his debut, and the Panthers should get Jaelan Phillips back. Nix hasn't challenged anyone down the field all year, and we don't expect that to start. That's the recipe for success, especially for a defense that wants to get downhill more with a new coordinator. Tetairoa McMillan returns to form There's a temptation to expect Tetairoa McMillan to see Pat Surtain more often than not and produce like he did against the Cleveland Browns, when the defense put its best corner on him and sent pressure. Why shouldn't the Browns repeat that? Well, they might, but as mentioned, the game plan should be better to offset that. And with Jalen Coker healthy, the Broncos won't be able to necessarily shade McMillan with Surtain 100% of the time. So, he should be able to bounce back. They're on the heels of a massive win over the rival Kansas City Chiefs that puts them in first place in the AFC West. The 28-24 win over the Chiefs also puts Denver in the hunt for home-field advantage. Yes, it's only eight games, but after the gauntlet the Broncos have faced, sitting at 6-2 and where they are is impressive. Now come the Carolina Panthers, who just got trucked on Thursday Night Football by the Green Bay Packers. As a result, the Panthers fired their defensive coordinator. Since Carolina plays in the NFC South, it leads the division at 3-4 and will be highly motivated to get back on track at home this Sunday. Denver is currently the -3-point road favorite at FanDuel Sportsbook. The total sits at over/under 43.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -118. Offensive Rankings Denver : Thirtieth in total offense (273.0 yards per game), 26th in rushing offense (92.6 YPG), 25th in passing offense (180.4 YPG), 22nd in scoring offense (21.5 points per game). Carolina : Ninth in total offense (363.7 yards per game), 22nd in rushing offense (102.0 YPG), fifth in passing offense (261.7 YPG), ninth in scoring offense (25.4 points per game). Defensive Rankings Denver : Twenty-fifth in total defense (355.3 yards per game), 25th in rushing defense (127.9 YPG), 20th in passing defense (227.4 YPG), 11th in scoring defense (20.6 points per game). Carolina : Twenty-third in total defense (349.6 yards per game), 30th in rushing defense (140.7 YPG), 10th in passing defense (208.9 YPG), 28th in scoring defense (27.6 points per game). Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Don't fall into the "trap" Sean Payton owns the NFC South. Dating back to his New Orleans Saints days, he knows the division and how to beat these teams. However, the Broncos have historically struggled in the early games on the East Coast. On top of that, Denver is coming off a brutal stretch of games and is on the heels of a ginormous win. Not to mention, the bye is after this Sunday's game. It's natural to take the foot off the gas and think, "We got this." In other words, the "trap game." Don't fall into that trap. It's imperative for the Broncos to remain focused on the task at hand. Build on the win over Kansas City with the goal of playing a complete game. — Ian St. Clair Score more points than Carolina My advanced analytics came through once again. For the 6th time this season, the Broncos have scored more points than their opponent and won. Following this trend, if they do that this Sunday against the Panthers, they will improve to 7-2. — Scotty Payne Scotty's analytics are spot on. One of the best ways to ensure his analytics remain proven correct is to limit the Panthers' ability to run the football. That forces Carolina into a one-dimensional attack and allows the defensive line to eventually pin its ears back and make Bryce Young as uncomfortable as the back of a Volkswagen. — Adam Malnati Keep feeding Jonah Coleman Good things happen when you run the ball effectively. We saw that for the Broncos in their past two victories. Last Sunday, rookie running back Jonah Coleman was solid on the ground for the Denver. He certainly deserves the majority of carries moving forward. The Panthers have one of the worst run defenses in the league and give up nearly 5 yards per carry. Why not pound the ball on the ground and keep giving Coleman a chance to prove himself even more? It seems like a great opportunity to see him shine. — Christopher Hart What are your keys to Sunday's game?

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Denver Broncos (6-2) head to Charlotte on Sunday looking to strengthen their hold on first place in the AFC West when they face the Carolina Panthers (3-4) at Bank of America Stadium. Although their record is a game below .500, the Panthers are also a first place team as they sit atop the NFC South. The Broncos have won four straight since a loss in early October at San Francisco. Carolina has suffered lopsided defeats in each of their last two games. This past Sunday, Bo Nix and the Broncos staged an impressive comeback to beat Kansas City, 28-24. Denver trailed 24-13 in the fourth quarter before Nix found Nate Adkins for a touchdown and Jaylen Waddle for the two-point conversion. After a missed Chiefs’ field goal, Nix connected with rookie Jonah Coleman for 51 yards, setting up Coleman’s go-ahead five-yard touchdown with 1:56 remaining. Denver then preserved the victory when its defense stopped Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs on fourth-and-goal. Nix finished 20-of-32 for 222 yards and two touchdowns. Denver has now won 15 one-score games over the past two seasons. As mentioned, Carolina has lost two straight, most recently losing at Green Bay last Thursday 27-19. The Panthers actually led 10-6 early in the second quarter behind a Chuba Hubbard touchdown, but Green Bay answered with 21 straight points to take control. Bryce Young completed 23 of 41 passes for 209 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Hubbard supplied 81 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries plus seven catches for 38 yards. Carolina made things interesting when Young hit Jalen Coker for a 26-yard touchdown with 5:37 left, but the Panthers failed on the two-point conversion and never scored again. The most troubling stats to emerge from the game was Young being sacked six times and Carolina’s offense managing only 258 yards. The central storyline is therefore strength against vulnerability: a Carolina offensive line that surrendered six sacks at Green Bay now has to protect Young against Denver, while the Panthers must find a way to slow a Broncos team that has developed a remarkable habit of winning tight games. Recent history strongly favors Denver. The Broncos hold a 7-2 all-time advantage over Carolina, including the postseason, and won the teams’ most recent meeting 28-14 in Denver on October 27, 2024. That game featured the same starting quarterbacks expected Sunday: Nix shredded Carolina for 284 yards and three touchdown passes, added a rushing touchdown and posted a 124.2 passer rating, while Young threw for 224 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. away.headline: Broncos' Week 9 injury report: WR Pat Bryant gearing up for return
away.blurb: After missing the last four games with an ankle injury, the Denver Broncos designated wide receiver Pat Bryant to return from injured reserve, opening his window to be activated to the 53-man roster. WR Courtland Sutton, meanwhile, was considered limited as he enjoyed a veteran rest day. Ditto for defensive end Zach Allen. Both will play against the Panthers. What's less certain is the Week 9 status of four key defensive players in safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring), defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike (shoulder), and cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle) — all of whom did not practice on Wednesday. Jones, Abrams-Draine, and Uwazurike were injured in Week 8 and their status for Sunday's contest is to be determined. They'd need to get in at least a few limited practices on Thursday and Friday to increase their chances of suiting up. Hufanga has been sidelined since Oct. 11 — he was initially expected to miss 2-3 games — and could be held out once more with Denver's Week 10 bye looming. This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/broncos/onsi as Broncos' Week 9 Injury Report: WR Pat Bryant Gearing Up for Return . That will likely happen sooner rather than later as Bryant was marked as a full practice participant on the team's first Week 9 injury report ahead of Sunday's road game at Carolina . Bryant was carted off the field amid Denver's Week 4 loss against the 49ers with what appeared to be a significant injury, though the second-year wideout avoided being placed on short-term injured reserve. Also listed as a full participant was Bryant's fellow pass-catcher, WR Jaylen Waddle, who's still nursing a minor chest issue. Waddle looked no worse for wear in last week's comeback victory over Kansas City , snagging three passes for 39 yards and a touchdown. A Potential Boost to Denver's Passing Offense Finally, the Broncos — if they choose to activate him this week — could be back at full strength in their receiving corps, with Waddle, Sutton, Bryant, Marvin Mims, and Troy Franklin all sharing the same field together. Bryant totaled nine receptions for 133 yards and a touchdown prior to going down, with his lone score coming in Denver's Week 3 upset of the Los Angeles Rams. He also snagged a two-point conversion earlier in the season. With sure hands and a wide catch radius, Bryant will again provide quarterback Bo Nix a security blanket over the middle of the field and in the red zone, helping to boost a passing offense that currently ranks 25th in the NFL, averaging 180.4 yards per game through the air. away.headline: Denver Broncos Injury Report Heading Into Week 8
away.blurb: Let's take a look at some of the injuries the Denver Broncos have dealt with throughout the 2026 NFL season, looking at both sides of the ball and who is out short- and long-term. Surtain suffered his ankle injury during Denver's Week 4 game against the 49ers and has been sidelined since. The All-Pro cornerback was a limited participant throughout Week 7 but returned to full participation this week. He carries no injury designation and is expected to return against Kansas City, which is a huge boost for the Broncos' defense. Hufanga, on the other hand, suffered his ankle injury during Denver's Week 5 victory over the Chargers and has missed the Broncos' last two games. He didn't practice this week and has been ruled out for Sunday's game. The Broncos have ruled out two players for Sunday's game and listed four others as questionable. Along with Hufanga, running back RJ Harvey has been ruled out after suffering a knee injury during the week. Harvey was added to the injury report Thursday as a limited participant but did not practice Friday. Defensive lineman Zach Allen, offensive tackle Garett Bolles, safety Brandon Jones and wide receiver Jaylen Waddle are all listed as questionable for Sunday's game. All four were limited participants Friday, and their availability will be determined closer to game day. We'll see if the Broncos can get back to full health for their huge divisional matchup against the Chiefs, but the biggest news for Denver this week is the return of Surtain, who immediately strengthens a Denver secondary that relies heavily on man-to-man coverage. He's well on his way toward earning another first-team All-Pro nod after securing the first such honor of his career last season. Waddle was hurt late in a Week 7 win over the Arizona Cardinals. Chiefs Demolished Broncos, Waddle in Week 1 The Chiefs opened the season with a 31-10 blowout win over the Broncos in Week 1 — a game in which Waddle had 1 reception for 2 yards on 3 targets. Not really what you want for a player the Broncos gave up a 1st-round pick for in a March trade with the Miami Dolphins . Waddle has grossly underperformed so far this year. Even though the Broncos are 5-2, Waddle has just 26 receptions for 276 yards and 1 touchdown — he's also struggled with drops to this point. home.headline: Injuries beginning to take their toll on the Panthers' secondary, offensive line
home.source: The Associated Press- Sports on MSN
home.blurb: “Just wanna see the guys connected,” Panthers coach Dave Canales said. "I just wanna see them excited about going out there and executing the plan. And playing fast, playing the physical brand. And the effort’s been there. Those things are right. But I know that we can make strides with being able to get everybody on the same page, tying in the whole unit.” Moton, the team's longtime right tackle, was able to return to action three weeks ago, but since injured his fibula and has been placed on injured reserve. Ekwonu is expected back in the next month or so. CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — The Carolina Panthers are probably wishing they could petition the NFL for another bye week. Mounting injuries to the secondary and offensive line have begun to take their toll on the Panthers (3-4), who have dropped two straight games and fallen into a tie with the Atlanta Falcons for first place in the NFC South. On Friday, the Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero after the team allowed Jordan Love to throw for 288 yards and three touchdowns in a 27-19 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Carolina entered the game last in the league in run defense. The Panthers promoted defensive line coach Todd Wash as interim defensive coordinator. Evero's fate may have been sealed when starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson went down in a Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns and were placed on injured reserve. Since then, the two cornerbacks who were replaced Horn and Jackson have suffered injuries. Akayleb Evans was placed on IR last week and Will Lee injured his hamstring against the Packers in the first half and had to leave the game. Canales said the injuries were taken into account when he fired Evero, but added that the decision was based on the big picture and “a lot of information." Things are just as shaky on the offensive line where the Panthers are playing without three starters, including tackles Taylor Moton and Ickey Ekwonu and guard Damien Lewis. Bryce Young was under constant pressure against the Packers. He was hurried 22 times, hit nine times and sacked six times. “We’ve got to make sure we do a good job of giving him solutions when they do have overloaded pressures and zero looks and things," Canales said. "But it wasn’t just that. They got after us with some four-man rushes and some stunts that we didn’t pass off well. That created a little bit of pressure there as well.” Rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling has struggled at right tackle this season. Running back Chuba Hubbard continues to be a bright spot for the Panthers despite playing behind an offensive line that has struggled to open holes. Hubbard was used extensively against the Packers and gained 81 yards on 22 carries while hauling in a team-high seven passes for 38 yards. He's clearly the only back offensive coordinator Brad Idzik trusts at this point in the season. home.blurb: According to the Broncos' official injury report, Hufanga remains sidelined by an ankle injury , while Jones is dealing with a hamstring issue. Neither player has been ruled out, but their availability remains uncertain. Hufanga has missed Denver's last three games since suffering his injury against the Los Angeles Chargers. The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-7 after falling to the Los Angeles Rams on the road in Week 8. Now the Chargers will have a chance to face off against the Houston Texans at home in Week 9. The Texans have found their fair share of struggles this season at 2-5, but they are fresh off of their annual bye and are well-rested for the matchup. The Bolts entered this week as 4.5-point underdogs, per FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under is currently set at 41.5 points. The Chargers struggled once again when facing the Rams. The Chargers had a 9-3 lead with 2 minutes to go in the second quarter, but they proceeded to give up a touchdown drive to close out the first half, which gave the Rams the lead going into the locker room. From there, the Rams capitalized and scored twice more in the third quarter to take a 24-9 lead, which ended up being the final score. Hope is not lost for the Chargers as they hold on to the No. 1 overall pick for the 2027 NFL Draft. However, getting a win or two would give them some morale for the second half of the season. Perhaps this will be the week the Chargers will have a chance to get their first win. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton Two of the league’s bigger disappointments meet Sunday afternoon at SoFi Stadium when the Chargers (0-7) host the Texans (2-5). Los Angeles is the only team in the NFL without a win and are as a result, firmly entrenched in the cellar in the AFC West. Houston sits in second in the AFC South but are three games behind the first place Jaguars. The Texans take the field following their bye week. They were last in action on October 25 when they lost a disappointing 27-21game in overtime at home to the New York Giants. Houston rallied from a seven-point fourth-quarter deficit to force overtime on C.J. Stroud’s 3-yard touchdown pass to Xavier Hutchinson with 52 seconds remaining. Stroud finished 17-of-28 for a season-low 153 yards and two touchdowns, while Woody Marks ran 19 times for 66 yards, but Houston produced only 237 total yards. The glaring issue was on defense. The Texans surrendered a season-high 188 rushing yards, including 124 and a touchdown to Cam Skattebo . The Chargers’ search for their first victory continues following their most recent game, a 24-9 loss last Sunday to the Rams. The Chargers had a 9-3 lead late in the first half but went scoreless over the final 38 minutes of the game. Justin Herbert completed 24 of 32 passes for 257 yards, but threw two interceptions, and the Chargers failed to reach the end zone for the second consecutive game. Los Angeles managed just 64 yards rushing with all nine Chargers’ points coming on Cameron Dicker field goals. The Chargers hold a narrow 6-5 advantage in the all-time series, but Houston has won the last two meetings, including two especially consequential victories. The Texans routed Los Angeles 32-12 in the AFC Wild Card round following the 2024 season, intercepting Herbert four times as Houston erased an early 6-0 deficit and ran away with the game. Houston then went back to SoFi Stadium in Week 17 last season and beat the Chargers 20-16, giving the Texans consecutive victories in the series for the first time. away.blurb: Multiple reports from on the ground noted that the dynamic defensive back's return to the practice field to begin Week 9. Still not practicing: #Texans Reed Blankenship (concussion protocol, hand surgery) and David Montgomery (groin) @KPRC2 https://t.co/vR5JeMfSaH pic.twitter.com/20aqSYpPpQ — Aaron Wilson (@AaronWilson_NFL) November 4, 2026 Houston Stressans (Garret Williams) called Pitre's return "massive" in a post on X. However, the offseason trade acquisition's timeline for return remained even more nebulous than Pitre's, a reality that the latter's presence at practice on Wednesday only intensifies. Houston Texans Get Good News About Versatile $39 Million Defensive Back Unlock the latest Heavy on Texans news — direct to your inbox. Houston Texans safety Jalen Pitre took a significant step on Wednesday. Safety Reed Blankenship also remained sidelined, per KPRC 2's Aaron Wilson on November 4. Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters on Monday that there was "no significant update" on either player and that "Everybody is still working their working their way back." Texans Get Jalen Pitre Back at Practice, David Montgomery Still Sidelined Ryans said they would see how their injured guys progressed throughout the week. There was optimism around Pitre before that, though, as Wilson reported on Monday that the fifth-year former second-round pick was "making steady progress" in his recovery. Likewise, there was optimism around Montgomery's recovery . "We all miss him a ton. Jalen gives us so much flexibility of what we're capable of doing on defense. We were able to stay nickel defense to whatever a team may throw at us, and we had our entire playbook at our disposal," Ryans said on " Texans Radio " in October. "When you miss a guy like that, it changes some things." Pitre's health has been the lone blemish against him. He has missed multiple games in every season logging all 17 starts during the 2022 regular season. The Texans signed Pitre to a three-year, $39 million extension that has him under team control through the 2028 season. away.headline: New Details Emerge on Texans DB Reed Blankenship's Injury
away.blurb: Not just their versatile nickel, Jalen Pitre, but also starting strong safety Reed Blankenship as well, who's been deemed out since he went down with a concussion during the second quarter of Houston's Week 6 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Sep 20, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Cincinnati Bengals running back Chase Brown (30) runs witht the ball as Houston Texans safety Reed Blankenship (6) defends during the first quarter at Reliant Stadium. We'll know more about Blankenship's status now and moving forward once the Texans are back practicing on Wednesday, and we get an injury report designating the veteran safety as a full, limited, or non-participant. A concussion absence typically lasts around one to three weeks for most players around the league, but with Blankenship's newly discovered hand surgery, there's a chance that it takes more time for him to return as a starter on the back end of the Texans' defense. For any time that Blankenship is set to remain out for the Texans' secondary, the name to keep an eye on will be veteran MJ Stewart, who returned from his lengthy absence due to a quad injury earlier this year, and was elevated to a starter last week against the Giants as a plug-and-play replacement. New Details Emerge on Texans DB Reed Blankenship's Injury Skip to main content SI.COM The Houston Texans have been without one of their starting safeties in their secondary for the past couple of weeks now. However, it was also revealed from the Texans' Week 7 injury report before facing the New York Giants that Blankenship was dealing with a hand injury –– one that wasn't exactly seen when the veteran safety went down against the Jaguars, but an issue that added to his troubles to get back on the field nonetheless. And it seems like, leading up to the Texans' Week 8 game against the LA Chargers, we now know a bit more about the status of Blankenship. What We Know About Reed Blankenship's Injury According to Jonathan M. Alexander of The Houston Chronicle , Blankenship had surgery on his left hand "not long after" the Texans' win over the Jaguars in Week 6. Alexander also notes that Blankenship is still in concussion protocol heading into the week against the Chargers, and will be a name to monitor as the week progresses. Texans safety Reed Blankenship, who remains in concussion protocol, also had surgery on his left hand not long after the Jaguars game, per a source. The Texans will see how he progress through the week. Blankenship was one of the Texans' biggest offseason additions brought in several months ago one a three-year contract, and was expected to bring an added sense of stability within an already strong Houston secondary. The team finds themselves at 2-5 following Week 8 of the season. That has them in second place in the AFC South and three games behind the Jacksonville Jaguars. In a reversal from last season, it is the team's defense that is holding them back. They are allowing 24.3 points per game (18th in NFL). Across five games this season, he has taken the ball 52 times for only 138 yards, resulting in a poor 2.7 yards per carry. During Week 5, the free agent acquisition pulled his groin in a game at the Tennessee Titans. He has been sidelined since. Moments after this transaction was reported, Houston head coach Demeco Ryans said he did not have any significant update on Montgomery's health. His status for Week 9 appears to be in jeopardy. picks.headline: NFL straight-up picks, Week 9: Packers-Patriots has us torn in otherwise chalky week
picks.blurb: The Thursday Night Football matchup pits a surging Jacksonville Jaguars team against a Baltimore Ravens squad forced to start an undrafted rookie at quarterback. The early slate Sunday includes a backup extravaganza between the New York Giants and Philadelphia Eagles as well as mismatches like Jets-Chiefs and Lions-Dolphins. But 4:30 p.m. Eastern? That's when we get to see which erstwhile contender might be for real when the Green Bay Packers face the New England Patriots. Sunday night brings the new-look Chicago Bears against a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team that didn't need to complete a single pass last week (OK, a bit of a stretch but should still be fun). And on Monday, Josh Allen takes on the league's best, most aggressive defense. That's made Week 9 a bit easier to predict, but it's not chalk across the board on our end. Welcome back to For The Win's straight-up, moneyline NFL picks column. I ended 2023 as Pickwatch’s top expert in a field of hundreds. The two seasons that followed? Ehhhhh, we don't like to talk about that. But I'm back and hopeful I'll either be good enough to rejoin the top 25 or, barring that, be so destructively bad you're left with no choice but to fade my picks all the way to prosperity. Joining me for 2026 is a six-person panel ranging from FTW editors (Charles Curtis, Wajih AlBaroudi and Jeff Smith) to betting analysts (Prince Grimes) to NFL writers (Robert Zeglinski, who is THRIVING this year, and Andrew Joseph). Here are our Week 9 picks. Jaguars at Ravens Bengals at Falcons Browns at Saints Cowboys at Colts Broncos at Panthers Lions at Dolphins Giants at Eagles Jets at Chiefs Rams at Commanders Texans at Chargers Cardinals at Seahawks Packers at Patriots Raiders at 49ers Buccaneers at Bears Bills at Vikings Season to date: Since our editing software occasionally struggles to make these picks super clear, here they are in an easier to read (but impossible to cut and paste) .jpg you can click to expand: Let's break out three games to talk about. Survivor pick of the week: Houston Texans (-4.5) over the Los Angeles Chargers We haven't burned Houston yet in my quest to turn what should be the easiest pick of the week into a coin flip. Now the Texans are coming off a bye and facing the shattered remnants of the Chargers on a home field that will be even more listless than usual in Los Angeles. DeMeco Ryans has a path from 2-5 to 6-5 over the next four weeks (against the Chargers, Browns , Colts and Ravens). He's not going to collapse on the first step. Last week : 1-0 Season to date : 4-4 Hardest favorite to back: New England Patriots (-3) over the Green Bay Packers Tom Brady returns to Foxborough, which Fox would like you to believe is a momentous occasion but isn't the first time he's been back to Gillette Stadium . The bigger story is two 5-3 teams have stabilized after iffy starts and a Drake Maye-Jordan Love shootout could be the best game of the year. Or, the Patriots' injuries could finally sink them back to "pretender" status. Why I like this pick : The Patriots have only lost once at home in the last 58 weeks (to the Buffalo Bills). Maye has been able to make adjustments on the fly, elevating targets like Eli Raridon, Pop Douglas and Kyle Williams the last few weeks with A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins all missing time due to injury. That includes a comeback effort in Week 8, albeit against a bad Miami Dolphins team. The Packers have the same problem many Matt LaFleur teams have had; they struggle to close out games. The run attack is a disaster. No one trusts Trey Smack with an end-of-half field goal at this point, let alone one that could decide a game in the fourth quarter. Why I don't like this pick : New England has yet to play a game without committing a turnover. Green Bay forces them more than all but one other team in the NFL. That leaves a top 10 defense to clean up a Patriot offense potentially missing its top three wideouts, its 1b running back and both its starting guards. The Patriots defense is solid, but not spectacular. Jordan Love is playing the best football of his life, taking shots downfield with incredible touch and accuracy. Granted, far too many of those throws wind up dropped, but that hasn't deterred him from taking risks capable of paying off in a massive way. Last week : 0-2 Season to date : 6-2 Upset pick of the week: Atlanta Falcons (+3) over the Cincinnati Bengals Last week's upset pick failed to account for a monsoon in Tampa. Still, it was worth it just to see Michael Penix Jr. throw more interceptions than the Buccaneers had pass attempts. AND YET, I AM ON THE FALCONS FOR A SECOND STRAIGHT WEEK. Well, let's unpack just how dumb I am. The Bengals keep touching the stove. Cincinnati just gave up 121 yards and two touchdowns to Tony Pollard and now has to face Bijan Robinson. That defense was the backdrop for the biggest game of Cam Ward's career and now has to face an angry Michael Penix Jr. who goes from rainstorms to the cozy confines of Madrid, which... huh actually I don't know how that's gonna affect things. The Falcons have quietly engineered a borderline top 10 defense and have only allowed 11 passing touchdowns this fall. That will place some of the onus on a run game that's underwhelmed behind the average efforts of Chase Brown. The Bengals' best win this season is over... the Buccaneers? The Lamar Jackson-less Ravens? The Dolphins or Titans? Ooooof, that resume. It's the Falcons. Joe Burrow just racked up about 1,000 yards on his own to fend off the Titans last week. The Cincinnati secondary is capable of shutting down a top-heavy receiving corps. It's the Falcons. picks.headline: Packers at Patriots: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 9 game
picks.blurb: The Patriots are likely to be on A.J. Brown watch once again. After the receiver missed Sunday's win over the Dolphins with a knee injury, Mike Vrabel said Monday that the team would need to see how Brown progresses before determinig his status for the upcoming tilt. Micah Parsons is expected to make his much-anticipated return to practice this week for the Packers, but he might still be a long way out from contributing. Matt LaFleur said the edge rusher might need the full 21-day window before being added to the active roster, which would mean a late November return. If there is any change to running back Josh Jacobs' disciplinary status, it won't come from the Packers. LaFleur said this week that the team plans to continue on with the ball carrier as the NFL extends its investigation. Patriots vs Packers odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Patriots -3.5 Moneyline: Patriots -160; Packers +145 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Patriots vs Packers USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Patriots 24, Packers 23 The Patriots are 17-0 with Drake Maye when favored by at least a field goal and we just may close there by Sunday afternoon. Who am I to disagree with a great trend? The Packers possess a dynamic passing offense but, even with Josh Jacobs back, still can't run the football with any efficiency. Plus, Christian Watson is dealing with a rib injury that sent him to the hospital for a portion of last week's primetime win over the Panthers. The Pats have the personnel to take advantage defensively, but Maye's offense also has questions around injuries to A.J. Brown, Hunter Henry and others. I'll take New England at home, but I'm expecting nervous pacing around living rooms throughout Massachusetts before this one is settled. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Packers 28, Patriots 27 Bombs away. With a matchup of two daring downfield passers and lackluster run games, both teams could air it out early and often against one another. Between their reliance on Jordan Love connecting on vertical shots and the pass rush picking up the rest of the defense with pressure, Green Bay might be more reliant of the two on igniting big plays. But the Packers' explosiveness shouldn't be doubted, and it could lead the team to its fifth win in six games. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Packers 26, Patriots 23 Good luck figuring these teams out. At times, Green Bay looks like a bad team. Then it looks like a Super Bowl contender. The same is true of New England, meaning there is a large range of outcomes we could see in Week 9. Will A.J. Brown play for the Patriots? Does it matter? Drop issues have plagued the star receiver and there's no sign of that disappearing anytime soon. On the other side, Christian Watson made 'Thursday Night Football” look like the WWE with his dramatic return. In the end, we'll trust the Packers offense to be the difference. away.headline: Packers get exciting injury update on Micah Parsons: Report
away.blurb: The Green Bay Packers expect superstar pass rusher Micah Parsons to return to practice next week, according to a report from NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport on Thursday. “Micah Parsons is expected to return to practice next week. Obviously short week, was not able to do it this week. Next week he should be on the practice field if all goes well. And that is an excellent thing for the Green Bay Packers,” Rapoport said. “I expect caution as far as when he’s actually on the playing field. They want to make sure everything around his knee is as strong as possible. “They are taking their time, but his return is coming.” The Packers will take the field for a “Thursday Night Football” matchup against the Carolina Panthers later this evening. Parsons’ next opportunity to return to the field for in-game action is a Week 9 matchup against the New England Patriots next Sunday. The Packers have been without their generational pass rusher for the entirety of the season thus far, as he continues to recover from the ACL tear he suffered in Week 15 of Green Bay’s 2025 campaign. Green Bay faces off against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 10 before taking their bye in Week 11. Thursday night’s matchup against the Panthers will kick off at 8:15 p.m. ET. away.headline: Is Matthew Golden playing tonight? Injury update for Packers WR
away.blurb: The 23-year-old had originally been listed as "questionable" due to shoulder and foot injuries, but he was able to suit up for his eighth game of the season. Golden logged a "limited" practice session on Wednesday after being listed as a non-participant in both Monday's estimated injury report and Tuesday's actual practice session. Packers coach Matt LaFleur was asked whether Golden would be available Thursday during a news conference on Tuesday, Oct. 27. LaFleur also pointed out that the nature of the short week would lead to most sessions being a walkthrough, so his players wouldn't get "any real reps" in advance of the game. The Green Bay Packers are preparing to take on the Carolina Panthers on " Thursday Night Football " in Week 8, marking the second time they have played an NFC South team on a short week this season. This time around, there are questions about whether the Packers will have one of their top wide receivers, Matthew Golden , at their disposal for the game. Golden is dealing with shoulder and foot injuries that have cast doubt on his availability for Thursday's game against the Packers. Golden has appeared in all seven Packers games so far in 2026. He has enjoyed a breakout season, tallying 36 catches for 540 yards and three touchdowns, though he has committed a league-high six drops. Here's what to know about Golden's status for the Packers' Week 8 game against the Panthers and how Green Bay may replace him if he cannot play. Is Matthew Golden playing tonight? Golden is officially active for the Packers' Week 8 "Thursday Night Football" matchup against the Panthers. Golden playing isn't a major surprise. NFL Media's Ian Rapoport provided a positive update on the second-year receiver during a Thursday, Oct. 29, appearance on "Good Morning Football." "I'm told he's trending towards playing," Rapoport said . "So, there's a good chance for the Packers that Matthew Golden does get on the field today." "I sure hope so," LaFleur responded . "But again, we're still kind of working through it." "We will have a short indie tomorrow, but to move guys around to see how they look," LaFleur said, describing the team's practice procedures. "But certainly hopeful for [Golden]." Who is Matthew Golden's backup? J. Michael Sturdivant is listed as Golden's primary backup on the Packers' official depth chart . The undrafted rookie from Florida has played sparingly through six games, notching three catches for 22 yards, all of which came in Green Bay's Week 3 loss to the Atlanta Falcons. But while Sturdivant is listed as Golden's backup, Savion Williams and Bo Melton have each logged more snaps than the Florida product. As such, those two may be more likely to fill in for Golden across from Christian Watson if the former Texas star can't play. home.headline: Adam Schefter makes admission on Patriots WR A.J. Brown's knee injury
home.blurb: Brown has been listed as having both an ankle and knee injury. He has missed multiple practices, and he also sat out the trip to Miami to face the Dolphins last week. Schefter explained that the knee issue is ultimately what kept Brown out last week, and it has created real concerns about his ability to contribute the way that the team hoped when they traded two draft picks, including a 2028 first-rounder, to get him from the Philadelphia Eagles . “It flared up. ...I know it says ankle and knee, but it’s the knee," Schefter said on ESPN's Get Up . "The knee held him out last week, and the knee is threatening to hold him out this week. It’s a knee that I think raises some concerns as to how long he’s gonna keep playing here in New England, and producing at a high level.” Comments reflect the views of their authors, not USA TODAY, its publications or its journalists. home.headline: AJ Brown's knee injury could jeopardize his long-term Patriots future
home.blurb: The New England Patriots have a big game against the Green Bay Packers coming up. With that in mind, it seems receiver A.J. Brown won't be ready to suit up. He was listed as a DNP on Wednesday's injury report with ankle and knee injuries. "It flared up… I know it says ankle and knee, but it’s the knee. The knee held him out last week, and the knee is threatening to hold him out this week. It’s a knee that I think that raises some concerns as to how long he’s gonna keep playing here in New England, and producing at a high level," Schefter said on Get Up. Regardless, Brown's knee is clearly a hurdle that New England will need to overcome. There's no telling how things will pan out, but there's a chance that knee injury will affect how his Patriots tenure plays out in the present and long term. Patriots have an A.J. Brown problem that they need to figure out ASAP ESPN's Adam Schefter added doubt not only this week but also about Brown's future in New England because of his knee injury. It's not ideal that his knee is forcing him to miss time. But the fact that Schefter said there are concerns about how long Brown will stick with the Pats has to be upsetting. Patriots may already regret trading for A.J. Brown Reports say Brown had a degenerative knee , but the Patriots' team doctors still signed off on a deal. That knee problem was an issue for other teams this offseason, and it's already popped up in New England. The Pats traded a 2028 first-round pick for Brown, wanting a true No. 1 WR for Drake Maye. Yet, it has been anything but that in 2026. He missed four games with a high-ankle sprain, but now he's likely to miss his second straight game with his knee. This knee injury won't go away. Instead, he will have to find ways to manage it. It's never great to have a player deal with a knee injury, but it hurts even more when it's your star receiver, whom you just traded for. A.J. Brown's knee injury creates an unsettling Patriots dilemma Receivers have to constantly cut, plant, and change directions to be at their best. And Brown's knee being an issue is worrisome. The Ole Miss product will also turn 30 in the offseason, and that's an age when teams believe players begin to decline. Not saying that will happen to Brown, since he's one of the league's top receivers when he's healthy. Still, there are concerns inside the building about his knee. The Pats believed he would be a staple on their offense for years to come, but now they doubt how long he'll last and how impactful he'll be. The Pats' bye week is in Week 11. New England may give Brown the next two games off (Packers & Lions), so he can rest that knee for four weeks and build for a second-half push. The only thing they can do is try to manage the workload and see if that helps. Ian Rapoport gives worst A.J. home.headline: Micah Parsons Headlines Initial Packers vs. Patriots Injury Report
home.blurb: Parsons was listed as a limited participant due to a knee injury, but he was far from the only Packers player listed. Both he and Chris Brooks are in their 21-day practice windows. Brooks was also listed as limited, as he's been dealing with an ankle injury. Other than those two, there were three other limited participants while four did not participate entirely. Franklin is dealing with a shin injury, Glover is dealing with a knee injury, Rhyan has issues with his ankle, and Whyle rounds things out with a concussion. In terms of limited participants, other than Brooks and Parsons, the following players popped up on the first injury report: At this point in time, it doesn't seem like Nixon will be ruled out for Week 9, but it's definitely something to monitor. Last but not least is none other than Watson, the man who had a WWE-style return from an ambulance on Thursday Night Football . Micah Parsons Headlines Initial Packers vs. Patriots Injury Report - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Micah Parsons Headlines Initial Packers vs. Patriots Injury Report (IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect) Jordon Lawrenz · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 1:12 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Of the nine Green Bay Packers players to appear on the Week 9 injury report , none has more hype surrounding them than Micah Parsons . No, Parsons will not be playing on Sunday, Nov. 8, against the New England Patriots. No, Parsons likely will not be back in time for a huge NFC North showdown on Sunday, Nov. 15, against the Minnesota Vikings. That said, Parsons has returned to practice, and that's all that matters. Currently in his 21-day practice window, the wheels are in motion for his expected season debut on Thanksgiving Eve against the Los Angeles Rams. Of course, GB still has a few games to focus on before getting to that point, and it all starts in Week 9 against the Patriots. As of Wednesday, Nov. 4, the following players did not participate: Offensive guard/tackle Travis Glover Offensive guard/center Sean Rhyan Banks joins the injured knee club alongside Glover and Parsons, while Nixon's groin injury could be catastrophic for the team. It comes as no surprise that Watson's name is on this list, especially knowing that he was coughing up blood after he broke a rib. Watson, similar to Nixon, should be good to go against the Patriots, but in no way do the Packers want to make him have a tougher week than he needs to.

Even Sunday's victory required the Raiders to overcome 33 points from the Jets. Purdy already has 1,748 passing yards and 15 touchdowns through seven games. Before the bye, he threw for 288 yards against Atlanta despite injuries affecting several important offensive contributors. The Raiders should expect Kyle Shanahan to test their coverage communication immediately. Motion, play-action and layered routes can create uncertainty without requiring Purdy to hold the ball for extended periods. My projection anticipates San Francisco attacking through the air even after establishing a lead. Rather than leaning exclusively on clock management, Shanahan will keep exploiting favorable matchups. That would require Las Vegas to build its passing plan around Bowers rather than waiting for him to emerge naturally within the progression. Quick throws would establish his involvement, while crossing routes and seam opportunities would provide the bigger gains. Kirk Cousins enters the matchup following a three-touchdown performance against the Jets, and his recent play has kept rookie Fernando Mendoza on the sideline. That continuity matters for this prediction. The Raiders can attack with an experienced quarterback rather than simplifying everything around a developmental transition. Bowers would become the central answer, particularly on third downs and near the goal line. His production will keep the Raiders competitive longer than expected, even as their defense struggles to match it. A 42–28 result would produce 70 total points, sailing past the opening 51.5-point total while giving San Francisco a 14-point winning margin. Ultimately, the difference will be possession-to-possession consistency. Cousins has been a bit of a revelation for the Raiders playing better than he has in the past couple of years. The veteran has thrown for 2,124 yards including 19 touchdowns against only five interceptions. Somewhat under the radar, the 49ers return from their bye week with a three-game lead in what was billed in the preseason as the best division in the NFL. Brock Purdy was an MVP candidate last season and is back in the mix this season having thrown for 1,748 yards including 15 touchdowns and only four interceptions. The injury came at MetLife Stadium against the Jets in Week 8, and it leaves the Raiders watching the sideline to see whether a key cornerback can come back. Jets quarterback Geno Smith hit wide receiver Garrett Wilson on a long completion to start the game, with accounts of the gain ranging from 31 to 41 yards. Porter hit the turf without being touched , according to the Las Vegas Review-Journal . Trainers helped Porter to the medical tent on the Raiders' sideline with the score still 0-0. He later emerged and was trying to regain his mobility under trainers' watchful eyes, according to Raiders beat writer Sam Warren. Why Isn’t Fernando Mendoza Playing for the Raiders Today? Insider Gives Timeline Las Vegas Raiders' Darien Porter Career Background Porter, 25, was born Jan. 6, 2001, in Bettendorf, Iowa, and is listed at 6 feet 2 inches and 195 pounds . He played receiver and cornerback at Bettendorf High School, catching 27 passes for 440 yards and seven touchdowns as a senior, and won a Class 4A state title in the 400 meters. He spent time at Iowa State from 2019 through 2024 , starting at receiver before moving to defensive back. Special teams made up most of his early role. He became a full-time starter in 2024, finishing with 18 tackles, two tackles for loss, three interceptions and two passes defended, and earned honorable mention All-Big 12 recognition. Porter ran an unofficial 4.30-second 40-yard dash at the NFL Scouting Combine. The Raiders selected Porter in the third round of the 2025 draft, 68th overall. As a rookie, he played all 17 games, starting 10 , and totaled 42 tackles, three passes defended and one fumble recovery. His rookie contract runs through 2028 . This season, Porter missed Week 2 against the Chargers because of a foot injury against the Dolphins in the opener. That was a separate issue from Sunday's injury. Before it, he had been targeted five times in that opener and allowed one catch for 12 yards , according to Pro Football Focus . Cox/Getty Images) Getty Cole Sullivan · HEAVY Thu, November 5, 2026 at 12:21 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The San Francisco 49ers weren't in action in Week 8, getting a much-needed and deserved bye week after their first seven games. San Francisco is sitting at 6-1 overall, but the team has dealt with a plethora of injuries all season long. The 49ers are set to host the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, looking to get back on track and maybe even welcome a few players back from injury. On Wednesday, head coach Kyle Shanahan provided San Francisco's first injury report of the week, addressing several notable players, including star running back Christian McCaffrey. 49ers Announce Injury Update on McCaffrey After exiting Week 7's matchup against the Atlanta Falcons with a hamstring injury before ultimately returning to finish the game, there seemed to be optimism that the injury wasn't serious heading into the bye. There still is no indication that anything has changed. However, Shanahan revealed that McCaffrey isn't practicing on Wednesday. The team will also have veteran wide receivers Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel sidelined on Wednesday, via Cam Inman of Bay Area News. For now, there is no cause for concern regarding his status for Sunday. How much he participates on Thursday and Friday will be a real indicator of whether he'll be ready to suit up against Las Vegas. If he can't go for some reason, rookie running back Kaelon Black would become the primary RB in Shanahan's offense. McCaffrey's 2026 Season With 49ers With all the injuries San Francisco has dealt with on the offensive side of the ball, McCaffrey has been one of the few consistent weapons for quarterback Brock Purdy. McCaffrey has played in every game, carried the ball 84 times for 389 yards and eight touchdowns, and caught 34 passes for 251 yards. home.headline: 49ers Injury Report: Three Stars Sit Out Practice, Two Key Players Return
home.blurb: 49ers Injury Report: Three Stars Sit Out Practice, Two Key Players Return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL 49ers Injury Report: Three Stars Sit Out Practice, Two Key Players Return Wide receivers Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring), Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) missed their last game on Oct. 25, which was a 29-20 loss to the Atlanta Falcons. Star running back Christian McCaffrey also suffered a mild hamstring strain during that game, and defensive end Nick Bosa wasn't able to return from a calf injury, despite previously being confident he would be able to play. Two key players could be nearing a return Bosa and Robinson returned to practice on Wednesday as limited participants, and wide receiver Christian Kirk (knee), linebackers Luke Gifford (groin) and Garret Wallow (hamstring), cornerbacks Nate Hobbs (groin) and cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder) and safety Marques Sigle (ankle) were also limited participants. Having Robinson and Evans back this Sunday would be a big shot in the arm for the Niners offensively, and if Bosa returns, they will be able to pressure Raiders veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins and challenge his limited mobility. Robert Marvi · Athlon Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 2:44 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The San Francisco 49ers' bye week is over, and they returned to practice on Wednesday. With a 6-1 record, things are looking rosy for them, but they're still dealing with injuries to key players. As far as injuries were concerned, it was a mixed bag for the Niners on Wednesday. Per 49ers Webzone, Evans, McCaffrey, Samuel, safety Siran Neal and left tackle Trent Williams didn't take part in practice on Wednesday. However, McCaffrey sounds confident that he can play this Sunday versus the Las Vegas Raiders. "It wasn't too bad," McCaffrey said. "I think having the bye week was awesome. Now, I feel great." Head coach Kyle Shanahan gave what sounded like a somewhat hopeful update on Evans. "I think we've made a lot of progress," Shanahan said, per Nick Wagoner of ESPN . "I think he's going in the right direction and it's something we definitely got to be smart with, but we're not going to overly do it. We just want to wait till he's healthy and he's still working his way to get there." Williams, meanwhile, had a veteran rest day. Robinson and Hobbs had their practice windows opened this week. Robinson hasn't played since Week 2, and Hobbs hasn't played at all this season. Lock -- a second round pick in the 2019 NFL Draft -- has a ton of starting experience in his career and has honestly outplayed Darnold in limited action in 2026. Oddsamakers still view the Seahawks as the clear favorite in this game, but it's notable that the line dropped so many points with Darnold out. Seattle takes on the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10, which will be Darnold's next chance to return to action. While there isn’t much positivity about the Seattle Seahawks from fans following the team’s blowout loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday, that hasn’t slowed confidence from oddsmakers ahead of their Week 9 game. According to the current odds on FanDuel Sportsbook , the Seahawks enter their second game against the Arizona Cardinals as 10.5-point favorites (-110) , with Seattle’s moneyline is set at -650 , while Arizona’s sits at +480 . The over/under line for the game is 44.5 , indicating that the Seahawks, now 4-4, are more than likely headed for another defensive slogfest against the Cardinals. The man trusted to score those points for the Cardinals will be none other than Washington State alum Gardner Minshew, who brought his patented good vibes to Arizona in the team’s second-half upset of the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8. Minshew ignited a spark in the Cardinals’ offense, which helped them score the most points, 33, that they’ve scored in a game all year. Arizona’s gutsy win in overtime against the Dallas Cowboys lifted them to 3-5 on the season. Aside from Minshew, running back Tyler Allgier had a career day after taking over for rookie Jeremiyah Love. The journeyman quarterback’s favorite target was Michael Wilson, who willed his team to a win with two broken ribs. The health of Wilson may be paramount to the Cardinals’ offense as he offers a second option for Minshew when superstar tight end Trey McBride is covered. While the Cardinals beat up on a reeling Cowboys’ defense, a trip to Seattle to play Mike Macdonald’s unit is an entirely different story. This unit held the Cardinals to 7 points in Week 2 and stifled much of Arizona’s run game. However, the story of these two teams’ early meeting was the Seahawks’ offense, which totaled 24 points in the second half after a slow start. Seattle, which was led by Drew Lock at the time, was led by their offensive engine, Jaxon Smith-Njigba. JSN totaled three touchdowns and 155 yards in that game, a performance the struggling Seahawks would love to see again. Unlike most of their games in 2026, the Seahawks had success on the ground in Week 2 with Emmanuel Wilson running for 92 yards and rookie Jadarian Price adding 52 yards. With Zach Charbonnet back, this matchup looks on paper to be the perfect bounce-back after they struggled to do much of anything on the ground against Chicago. away.headline: Ravens to trade for Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals to fill QB void: Report
away.blurb: Ravens to trade for QB Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals: Report – NBC New York Skip to content Main Navigation Search Search for: Weather Baltimore lost Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to potential season-ending injuries last week. By Logan Reardon • Published November 4, 2026 • Updated on November 4, 2026 at 3:15 pm Jacoby Brissett of the Arizona Cardinals warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Nov. 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. There's a new quarterback in Baltimore. Days after Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley suffered potential season-ending injuries , the Ravens reportedly traded for veteran Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the news on Wednesday, adding that the trade is expected to be finalized over the weekend. Watch NBC 4 free wherever you are With the Ravens playing on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the earliest that Brissett could make his debut for the team would be on Monday, Nov. 16, against the Los Angeles Chargers . Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will start for Baltimore against Jacksonville, with inexperienced quarterbacks Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis serving as the backups. Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and two turnovers in his relief debut Sunday against the Buffalo Bills after Jackson and Huntley went down. The two-time MVP Jackson, coming off three missed games with an ankle injury, suffered a thumb injury that will require surgery on his first throw last Sunday. His backup, Huntley, returned to the field, but he went down with a turf toe injury that will require surgery in the second quarter. Brissett, 33, lost his starting job to Gardner Minshew on Sunday. That made him an obvious trade candidate before next Tuesday's deadline, and the Ravens pounced quickly. Brissett started Arizona's first eight games this season and went 3-5 with 1,719 passing yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Carson Wentz to start for Vikings vs. Bills with Kyler Murray ‘week-to-week' An 11-year NFL veteran, Brissett has several ties to the Ravens' coaching staff. Quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork held the same position for the Cardinals last season and passing game coordinator Marcus Brady was a Colts assistant when Brissett was there from 2018-20. Brissett was drafted in 2016 by the New England Patriots and has gone on to play for six teams before Baltimore -- the Patriots (2016, 2024), Indianapolis Colts (2017-20), Miami Dolphins (2021), Cleveland Browns (2022), Washington Commanders (2023) and Cardinals (2025-26). home.headline: They didn’t have to tell us that, definitely unusual — NFL analyst questions Seahawks’ decision to reveal Sam Darnold’s surprise injury
home.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks will be without Sam Darnold for their Week 9 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, but the timing of the team’s announcement seems questionable to some, especially given its decision to disclose the quarterback’s injuries. “So they got a lot of faith in Drew Lock. I just think that this idea that Wednesday, out of the blue, they tell us that Sam Darnold is out with a quad injury. They tell us that he’s week to week, which usually means you’re going to miss a couple of weeks. They didn’t have to tell us that,” Florio said. “Now I appreciate the transparency, because what they could have done, they could have just put him down as did not practice. They could have done that yesterday. They could have done it today. They could have done it tomorrow, and then they could have called him out on Friday,” the analyst continued. Drew Lock is expected to start against Arizona, although his availability for Seattle is not settled. The veteran is managing a right-elbow injury and was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated injury report after Seattle held a walkthrough. Darnold, meanwhile, is considered week-to-week and has not been placed on injured reserve. The cracked rib could potentially be managed while playing, but the quad injury is expected to keep him out against Arizona. Coach Mike Macdonald confirmed Wednesday that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game because of a quad injury suffered late in Seattle’s 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears. Mike Florio Questions Seahawks’ Decision To Announce Sam Darnold’s Absence Early While the coach disclosed the injury, Macdonald also revealed that the quarterback had played through a cracked rib for nearly the entire game. Darnold suffered the injury on the second play against Chicago after taking a hard hit from blitzing cornerback Kyler Gordon. He did not report the issue to the coaching or medical staff during the game and continued playing through the final whistle. He finished with two touchdown passes despite the injury, and Seattle’s coaches and medical staff did not learn about the cracked rib until after the game. The decision to reveal the extent of Darnold’s injuries, however, prompted NFL analyst Mike Florio to question why Seattle chose to announce the quarterback’s absence on Wednesday rather than wait until later in the week. Speaking on “NFL on NBC” with Chris Simms, Florio said the Seahawks could have followed the league’s injury reporting rules without immediately confirming that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game. “But they decided to just lead with their chin on this, which I thought was strange. It’s definitely unusual, and it forfeits the uncertainty that the Cardinals would have as to who they’re getting ready for. Now they know they’re getting ready for Drew Lock or Jalen Milroe,” Florio added. Chicago has not lost a game that Williams has started and finished this season (4-0), and it upset the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night in Week 8. Perhaps public perception pushes this to a touchdown and beyond later in the week. The Chicago Bears have a short turnaround to come down from a statement win at Seattle on Monday night. Chicago looked strong on both sides of the ball, especially a new-look defense with DL Jeffery Simmons causing chaos up front. Tampa Bay poses a bigger threat on the ground than the Seahawks' punchless rushing attack, allowing the Bucs to dominate the football and keep Caleb Williams & Co. on the sidelines. The Buccaneers rode their running backs to victory in a rain-soaked matchup with Atlanta in Week 7, rumbling for 324 yards on the ground. But even before that weirdo result, Tampa was a top-tier run game in EPA per handoff, DVOA and run block win rate.
