picks.blurb: Buccaneers vs. Bears bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Buccaneers vs. Bears bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 6:02 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Chicago Bears meet on Sunday Night Football with very different momentum and very different identities. Tampa Bay just beat Atlanta 16–0 without completing a pass. Chicago comes in off an upset of Seattle. The Bears are 6-point favorites, and the total is 46.5. The Bucs have won three of their last four after an 0–4 start, so they are still in the NFC South race. These predictions lean on the contrast between Tampa Bay's run-first plan and Chicago's explosive offense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Caleb Williams leads the Bears past 30 points again Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Chicago will score at least 30 points, and Williams will account for three touchdowns. The Bears have scored 30 or more in every game Williams has finished this season, and they have not lost one he has started and finished (4–0). Since he returned from his hamstring injury, they have not trailed in any of three games. Williams threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns in a 30–24 win over New England. Chicago's pass offense averages 236.4 yards a game compared with 131.4 for Tampa Bay. That edge in the air is the core of this call. Tampa Bay's pass defense gives up 205.9 yards a game, which leaves room for chunk plays. Chicago's offense ranks 10th in EPA per play despite Williams missing three full games. I expect him to throw for at least 275 yards and add a rushing score. The one wrinkle is the Bears' backfield. Running back Kyle Monangai is listed as out with a thumb injury, which could shift more of the offense to Williams. Tampa Bay runs for 200 yards and still loses The Bucs will pile up another 200 rushing yards, and it still won't be enough. Against Atlanta, Tampa Bay ran 56 times for 324 yards. Bucky Irving gained 170 yards on 27 carries, and Kenny Gainwell added 140 on 25. Baker Mayfield attempted only three passes in steady rain. Chicago's run defense is beatable, allowing 4.4 yards per carry. Tampa Bay ranks eighth in EPA per rush, so the ground game will work on Sunday night. The problem is what happens when Chicago scores early. The Bucs average 22.3 points a game. A team rated poorly through the air can't easily come back against the best third-down defense in football, according to one projection. I'm projecting 200 rushing yards because the Bears' run defense can't stop everything. But Tampa Bay's offense needs scoring drives, not just yards, and the run game alone won't produce 30 points. Injuries make it harder. Gainwell is questionable with a hip issue, and outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was trending toward out. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka was inactive last week with a foot injury and is also a concern. Mayfield throws 35 passes and the Bears win 34–20 The game ends with Chicago winning 34–20, and Mayfield forced into a very different afternoon than the one in Tampa. A 34–20 final would add up to 54 points, clearing the 46.5 total comfortably, and it would give Chicago a 14-point cover. Mayfield returned from a fractured thumb two games ago and is still working back to full rhythm. He has 679 passing yards and three touchdowns on the season, so asking him to throw 35 times is a real shift for this offense. That volume creates risk. If Chicago leads by two scores in the third quarter, Tampa Bay has to abandon the run and put the ball in Mayfield's hands. I expect two interceptions, including one that sets up a Chicago touchdown. The Bucs will compete. They'll move the ball, their kicker has been perfect this season and their defense will make a few plays. But the Bears' offense is more dangerous, and they are better built to play with a lead. picks.headline: Week 9 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Bears have momentum going into Sunday night vs. Buccaneers
picks.blurb: Week 9 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Bears have momentum going into Sunday night vs. Buccaneers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, November 5, 2026 at 7:30 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Chicago Bears hype is about to get very loud. This NFL season seems wide open. There isn't one great team yet and there are few trustworthy contenders who have emerged. The Bears seemingly saw it the same way when they traded two first-round picks for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. And through one game, it seems like a transformative trade. The Bears had a fantastic performance on a national stage, shutting down the Seahawks in a 34-17 win . Chicago's Super Bowl odds took a leap, as did Caleb Williams' MVP odds. In a season dying for a dominant team to emerge, maybe it's Chicago. The Bears' offense isn't a question. It has scored 30 points in every game Williams has started and finished (it did score just three points against the Vikings and Williams played three-and-a-half quarters, but that says something about Minnesota's defense). If Simmons has as big of an impact on the defense as it appeared on Monday night, Chicago will be looking really good. Nobody paying attention to the NFL hadn't seen how dominant Simmons is, but it was still impressive to see how quickly he fit in and made plays. Chicago gets another close-up in prime time this week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night. Surprisingly, the Buccaneers are far better analytically than their 3-5 record would suggest. They're fifth in DVOA , eight spots ahead of the Bears, and eight in net EPA (expected points added) per play. The Bears are strong in net EPA, coming in third. The Buccaneers will be completely overshadowed in this game. The Bears will be the focus on Sunday night as they've emerged as one of the NFL's most dangerous teams. That's a reason they're a healthy 6.5-point favorite. That's a lot of points, and the Buccaneers might be secretly pretty good. That's why Buccaneers +6.5 is the pick. And if the Bears blow out Tampa Bay in a big prime-time window, they'll take over as the talk of the NFL, if they're not already. The Bears are 4-0 in games that Caleb Williams started and finished this season. Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 9 of the NFL season: Jaguars (-10) over Ravens Even at -10, the line seems too low. The Jaguars have three wins by 24 points or more and two came against the 5-3 Browns and the 5-3 Patriots. They're good. There could be a letdown facing Baltimore undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano, and it's possible the Ravens rally around Fagnano for a season-saving performance with Jacoby Brissett on the way next week. But this seems like a huge ask for the Ravens, who have scored 13 or fewer points in three straight games. Bengals (-3) over Falcons The Bengals and Falcons go to Madrid, Spain, for this one. The Falcons are nearly impossible to figure out. They followed up a win over the undefeated 49ers by losing to a Buccaneers team that didn't complete a pass. That sums up Atlanta's season. We should trust Joe Burrow, who is on a heater, though there are more questions about Cincinnati's defense after it gave up 36 points to the Titans at home last week. Giants (-3) over Eagles Maybe Joe Milton III gives Philadelphia a boost and the Eagles get their first win since Week 2. But since Jalen Hurts went on IR, the Eagles have lost all three games by double digits. It's not a good team in any way, and Milton is far from a sure thing. The Giants are off a bye and should be feeling good coming into this one. Panthers (+2.5) over Broncos The Broncos are the better team. A few things work against them in this spot: It's an early start on the East Coast, and the Panthers have three days rest advantage. The Broncos are also coming off an emotional win over the Chiefs and there could be a letdown. Denver has been much better at home this season. Carolina has faded after a good start but this is a decent opportunity for a win. Dolphins (+7) over Lions Give Miami credit for playing hard. Maybe at some point that effort starts to fade, but the last time they truly got blown out was Week 2. They lost by 14 points to the Chiefs, but Kansas City led by only seven points with three minutes left. It's possible the Lions score enough to cover, but remember that they're usually a different team outdoors. Chiefs (-10) over Jets Kansas City will enjoy the breather after facing the Seattle and Denver defenses on the road the past two weeks. This seems like the type of game in which the Chiefs could take out their frustrations on an opponent that does have some talent but has won only once since Week 1. Saints (-3) over Browns The Browns are likely going with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback because Deshaun Watson was put in concussion protocol. It's not like Watson was playing so well he's irreplaceable, but Sanders has thrown only three passes all season. The Saints are well rested coming off a bye. The Saints are not a great team this season, but this might be a spot for them to get right. Rams (-5.5) over Commanders Is it time to trust the Rams? They have covered two games in a row without a sweat. Those wins came against mediocre (Raiders) or bad (Chargers) teams, but they did handle business. And the Commanders are mediocre at best and maybe just bad. Let's see if the Rams are truly back. Cowboys (-5.5) over Colts It is incredibly hard to trust the Cowboys, especially as a road favorite. But what we saw from the Colts last week in a 42-7 loss was troubling. There was no fight left in that team, which has lost key players to trades and knows its season is done. This could be a bad mistake, trusting a defense that can't stop anyone to cover almost a touchdown on the road. Taking the Colts at this point is even harder. Texans (-4.5) over Chargers It's a lot for Houston to be favored by this much on the road, however, home-field advantage has been mostly eliminated this NFL season and the Chargers have no home-field advantage — even if that was still a thing. Houston is coming off a bye and still has hopes to revive its season. The Texans still have a 34.4% chance to make the playoffs according to DVOA. The Chargers are 0.0% on that list. They'll cover a spread at some point but it's hard to anticipate when it happens. Raiders (+10) over 49ers The Raiders have four losses, and they came against four of the better teams in the NFL: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills and Rams. The bad news is this week they get the Super Bowl favorites. The 49ers should be getting many players back after their bye. But the Raiders can move the ball and they're getting a lot of points. Seahawks (-8.5) over Cardinals With all the quarterback chaos this week, we get two teams that had a different quarterback in Week 8. Brissett was benched and traded, and Gardner Minshew II takes over. Sam Darnold has a quad injury and he'll be out, with Drew Lock taking over. Lock is a reasonable replacement, and Minshew isn't facing the Cowboys defense this week. Packers (+3) over Patriots The Patriots have a lot of injuries and the Packers have a few days of extra rest. In a game that seems evenly matched, the small edges add up. Green Bay started the season very slow but has looked much better over the last four games, winning three and barely losing at Detroit. New England has also emerged after an early-season slump to win four of five. This is a really fun matchup, and even enough to feel OK taking the points. Vikings (+3.5) over Bills This is an interesting game because the teams have opposite strengths. The Bills have a great offense and bad defense, and the Vikings have a bad offense and great defense. The Minnesota defense held the Bears to three points after all; Chicago has scored 30 points in every other Caleb Williams start. It will be a great test against Josh Allen, who is having another fantastic season. It's never enjoyable to be going against Allen, but getting 3.5 points with a defense this good seems right … as long as the offense does at least a little bit. Wow, the Bears look good. Ben Johnson, Caleb Williams, and their Chicago Bears seem like they are on a collision course for a deep playoff run in 2026. So yes, the Bears are hot— Steaming, but so are the Buccaneers. Tampa Bay is coming off two-straight wins, three of their last four and has seemingly found their new formula for offensive success. Will those good vibes and momentum carry over into the Chicago night on Sunday Night Football? " Battles are won in the trenches, in the grit and grime of courageous determination. " How can the Buccaneers win? Be the line they claim to be. TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Graham Barton #62 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers blocks against Kendal Daniels #53 of the Atlanta Falcons during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears are no joke and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers will need to be all the way buttoned up to be able to stay with Chicago in this game. The Bears have a lot of things going for them in 2026, but their most recent addition may be the scariest. Chicago's highly publicized trade for Jeffery Simmons opened some eyes when they made it. For those who haven't seen may Titans' games over the years, Monday night may have opened some more— Simmons is in the elite class of football players in the NFL and after spending years on a losing team, he looks motivated and rejuvenated. The trade for Simmons was an all-in move, the kind of move teams make when they have one goal on their mind— The Bears are a Super Bowl or bust team. The trade paid immediate dividends, Simmons' first game with Chicago was a watch what I can do performance as he snared a team-leading six tackles (two for a loss) and a sack. For the Buccaneers, this game will be the game where their offensive line needs to prove the last two weeks true. Tampa's season began horrifically, 0-4, a quarterback injury, and more importantly for the sake of this discussion, an offensive line that was woeful. Tampa Bay's offensive line came into the season projected to be one of the strongest units on the team, perhaps in the league, depending on who you asked. Through the first four games, the Buccaneers allowed 20 sacks. Baker Mayfield spent most of those first four games running in circles behind the line of scrimmage like Fran Tarkenton, until he ran himself into an injury. In the four since, Tampa's only surrendered seven sacks with five of the seven coming against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Tampa Bay will be and should be the underdog on Sunday. If there is any chance that an upset is in the cards they will need to protect their quarterback. Baker Mayfield is going to have to attempt more than three passes in this game to lead the team to victory and he will need to be upright to do so. Chicago has an absolute game-wrecker on their defense, he will make his plays— The Bucs can't expect to wipe Jeffery Simmons out of the game, however, they cannot allow the game to devolve into what fans saw earlier in the season from this offensive line, Baker Mayfield, and the passing game. " You can't stop him, you can only hope to contain him ." How can the Buccaneers lose? Lose contain of Caleb Williams. Caleb Williams might not be a truly great quarterback, though he does seem to be enroute to that status in short order, but he is a truly special athlete. No, he isn't running 4.2 40's or leaping 13' in a broad jump but he is as all around dynamic as they come. One of the issues Tampa Bay might have is Williams simply does not throw interceptions. Caleb has missed some time this year, but he has only thrown one interception— Last year, just seven. Williams' lack of interceptions isn't even a Ben Johnson related statistic because dating back two years ago, pre their union, Williams tossed just six while throwing 20 touchdowns for a better than 3:1 touchdown to interception ratio. In his career (three years), Williams has thrown less interceptions than Baker Mayfield did in 2024—Turnovers may be off the table. Another key issue that Caleb Williams presents is his elite management of the pocket. Williams is not a runner, but he is quite mobile. He has a phenomenal ability to majestically glide up, back, or out of the pocket towards free space and away from danger . Todd Bowles and the Buccaneers' defense will need to work tirelessly to mitigate that on Sunday night. Williams will dagger the Bucs with big plays off script if they let him. Bowles and the Bucs have been somewhat of mixed bag against mobile quarterbacks, different matchups bringing about different results, but Caleb Williams will represent a very unique challenge. Williams is not just looking to move around the pocket to buy time to throw— He isn't just looking break out of the pocket so that he heave the ball down field on a broken play— He won't be looking to run outside of contain so that he can scramble for yards to move the chains— Caleb Williams will be looking to do any and all of the above. He is special and he has proven that he can do each and every one of those things on any given play— Meaning, the Buccaneers must be dialed into the details on their rushes, sound in their tackling, and if they are caught lacking and take even just one snap off Williams could gash them for a game changing play. Todd Bowles' defense has been reliably solid in 2026, as of late they've been exemplary. Sunday night's game against Chicago will be a true test. Caleb Williams has the ability to put a defense on a poster, he and Ben Johnson have left a decent amount of carnation in their wake. Can Tampa Bay contain Caleb Williams and stay off his highlight reel?

Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. picks.headline: Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football
picks.blurb: Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Two 6-1 teams enter Monday Night Football with very different questions. Can the Buffalo Bills keep rolling against the NFL's stingiest defense? Can the Minnesota Vikings generate enough offense to avoid wasting another strong defensive performance? Buffalo visits U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9 following a 36–10 victory over Baltimore. Minnesota returns home after Detroit ended its unbeaten start with a 19–15 win. The Bills opened as three-point favorites, setting up a compelling clash between offensive firepower and defensive disruption. These three predictions anticipate a departure from Minnesota's usual defensive script, explosive passing, costly mistakes and a dramatic finish that hands Buffalo its second defeat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Justin Jefferson explodes for 175 yards and two touchdowns Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Jefferson will deliver the performance Minnesota has been waiting for, finishing with at least 175 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Jefferson caught five passes for 33 yards and a touchdown against Detroit and enters Week 9 without a 100-yard receiving game. Buffalo presents an opportunity to change that. Its defense ranks 30th against the pass, making this a matchup Minnesota should attack rather than approach conservatively. The Vikings need to manufacture touches before asking Jefferson to win difficult downfield assignments. Motion, condensed formations and crossing routes would help create cleaner releases and give the quarterback defined throwing windows. The bigger gains should follow when Buffalo adjusts to those shorter completions. One double move or broken coverage could turn a productive evening into a spectacular one. Quarterback availability remains important. Kyler Murray is managing hamstring tightness , with Carson Wentz the likely alternative if Murray cannot play. Expect Minnesota to make its best receiver the centerpiece, not merely a name opponents must account for. Josh Allen accounts for four touchdowns but commits three turnovers Allen will produce enough spectacular plays to keep Buffalo dangerous and enough mistakes to give Minnesota control of the outcome. The bold prediction is four total touchdowns alongside three turnovers, including at least two interceptions. https://twitter.com/search?q=josh%20allen&src=typed_query&f=top Minnesota's defense provides the foundation for that aggressive forecast. Entering Week 9, the Vikings lead the league in points allowed per game at 13.3, quarterback pressure rate at 45.8 percent and sack percentage at 10.96 percent. Pressure alone will not neutralize Allen. His ability to escape the pocket can turn a successful blitz into a defensive emergency, particularly when coverage players must chase receivers across the field. That creates the central tension. Minnesota will win several snaps decisively, but Allen will punish a few failed pressure attempts with explosive completions or scrambling opportunities. The turnovers will come when he tries to rescue plays that should end with a throwaway. Disguised coverage behind an apparent blitz can invite exactly that kind of aggressive decision. Buffalo's offensive line also bears watching. Right tackle Spencer Brown's availability is a concern entering the matchup, potentially complicating protection against Minnesota's pressure packages. Allen will remain the game's most dangerous improviser. On this night, improvisation will carry a substantial price. Minnesota wins 38–35 on a last-second field goal The final bold prediction ties those individual performances together: Minnesota wins a shootout with a field goal as time expires. A 38–35 result would produce 73 points, comfortably exceeding the opening total of 46.5. It would also represent a dramatic departure from the Vikings' defensive scoring average. The logic is not that Minnesota suddenly becomes a bad defense. Turnovers and explosive plays can produce points without requiring long, methodical drives. Jefferson's breakout keeps the Vikings moving, while Allen repeatedly answers before one late mistake gives Minnesota the deciding possession. After losing its unbeaten record, Minnesota will respond with its most convincing offensive statement and a victory that reinforces its place among the league's contenders. picks.headline: Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills
picks.blurb: Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Minnesota Vikings Receive Bold Prediction for Game Against Buffalo Bills (Gregory Fisher-USA TODAY Sports) Joey Hickey · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings (6-1) have a pivotal matchup on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. And while losing the game wouldn't make them a pretender, winning the game could solidify the Vikings as contenders. Minnesota has played great defense through seven games, but the offense has been lacking. Now, fans are looking for the team to show improvement on offense. If it doesn't happen, we could see the team explore changes on offense. Vikings Wire's Andrew Harbaugh predicts that Vikings backup quarterback Carson Wentz will see playing time in Monday night's game against the Buffalo Bills. Here's some of what Harbaugh had to say about his chances to take the field for Minnesota in the game. "Kyler Murray has played poorly enough this season and has not shown a real grasp of the offense or the players' tendencies within it. Carson Wentz has not been a rockstar, but he has been more than serviceable for the Vikings when he has played. I predict that the first half could be rough for the Vikings' offense, and at halftime Kevin O'Connell tries to give the offense a spark with a quarterback change." Harbaugh adds that it could be a breakout day for another Vikings player. He has star Vikings wideout Justin Jefferson catching two touchdown passes in the matchup. Here's what he had to say on the breakout. "Justin Jefferson has started to be a bit more vocal about how he feels about the offense being so quiet. I think they make it a point to get him going early in the game, and then by the end of the night he has two touchdowns. They have to get him involved more; the offense goes as Justin Jefferson goes, after all. If they do not use him more soon, then ideas and outside voices are going to start getting louder." Jefferson's frustrations have drawn questions about the player throwing him the football. It's not surprising that there have been questions given all the pieces that the Vikings have on offense. It's not that starting quarterback Kyler Murray has been awful. The offense has been awful, though. Some believe a change at quarterback is necessary to bring a spark. Maybe a change at quarterback isn't the fix, but something will need to change for the offense to start moving the football. If it doesn't the Vikings will have squandered what could be one of the NFL's best defenses of the last decade. We'll keep a close eye on what moves head coach Kevin O'Connell makes when the matchup gets underway with Buffalo.

picks.blurb: NFL Insider Makes Bold Prediction About Vikings Offensive Direction in Week 9 vs. Bills - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football TNF: Jaguars-Ravens preview Wemby makes NBA history Ronaldo retires from Portugal Luka gets fan booted First CFP rankings Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kevin O'Connell has spent the week calling Kyler Murray his starter, but a hamstring may make that call for him. NFL Network insider Tom Pelissero said Thursday on KFAN's Power Trip Morning Show that he expects Carson Wentz to start for the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings against the Buffalo Bills on Monday night, days after Murray struggled through the loss in Detroit . "I would lean toward it being Carson Wentz," Pelissero said on KFAN . He described the hamstring as legitimate but not major, and said Minnesota may not want to risk a quarterback who relies on his legs at less than full speed. Carson Wentz has already won two games Nov 1, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell talks to quarterback Kyler Murray (1) during the third quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field.Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Wentz isn't a stranger to this offense. He played most of the 39-22 opener against Green Bay after replacing Murray early and threw three touchdown passes, then started the 9-3 win in Chicago. He has 276 passing yards and no interceptions this season, and Minnesota won both games. Those wins weren't pretty, though. The offense scored nine points at Soldier Field, and Wentz was sacked six times across the two games. Behind a line that has allowed 21 sacks, the Vikings would be trading mobility for a quarterback who has to get the ball out on time. Murray has 1,022 passing yards, five touchdown passes and three interceptions, and he's been sacked 15 times. He has also run for 167 yards on 29 carries, which is why a sore hamstring matters more for him than it would for most quarterbacks. O'Connell said Monday he isn't considering a performance benching and Murray is still the starter when healthy, per ESPN. "I don't think we're there yet," he said of a possible absence , adding that he would keep getting updates from the medical staff. Pelissero's take lands after Nick Kostos argued the Vikings can't keep waiting on Murray . Pelissero also said he sees a low chance of a major trade before the Nov. 10 deadline, which leaves the job between the two quarterbacks already in the building. Either one draws a tough assignment. Buffalo's Greg Rousseau has seven sacks, and Josh Allen brings the NFL's most efficient offense to U.S. Bank Stadium, so Brian Flores' defense may need to carry the night again. O'Connell's Thursday press availability should offer the next clue. Our friends from the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the betting lines for Week 9 around the National Football League, and the Vikings have opened as a 3-point underdog to the Buffalo Bills for their Monday Night Football matchup. The over/under for this one is currently sitting at 46.5 points. The Vikings' lack of offensive prowess finally caught up to them in Week 8 against their NFC North rivals from Detroit. Minnesota held the high-flying Lions' offense to just 19 points, but their inability to put points of their own on the board kept their defense on the field for extended periods of time, and eventually Detroit's run game wore them down en route to a 19-15 victory over the Vikings at Ford Field. The Bills will come into this one on a three-game winning streak. So, in a matchup between the NFL's #1 offense and the league's #1 defense, it's the offense that will come into the game as the favorite. home.blurb: Report: Vikings may be without Kyler Murray for MNF clash with Bills - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Report: Vikings may be without Kyler Murray for MNF clash with Bills Chris Trapasso · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 5:16 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The week after facing a backup and third-string quarterback, the Buffalo Bills defense might see the Vikings backup at quarterback on Monday Night Football . On ESPN's Get Up Thursday morning, Adam Schefter hinted at a strong likelihood Carson Wentz will be Minnesota's starter in Week 9's game: Regarding Kyler Murray, Schefter said, "clearly his status for Monday night, is at best, up in the air. And it sounds like it is trending toward Carson Wentz starting on Monday night." Murray is laboring through a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 8's loss to the Lions. On the season, Murray is completing 64.9% of his passes at 6.6 yards per attempt with five touchdowns to three interceptions. He's also run 29 times for 167 yards. In non-garbage time situations, the Vikings are 26th in football in EPA per dropback entering this game. Wentz has appeared in two games in 2026 — one relief appearance, one start. Collectively in those contests, the veteran completed 23-of-39 attempts for 276 yards (7.07 yards per) with three touchdowns and no interceptions. All three touchdowns came in his Week 1 relief appearance at home against the Packers, which amounted to a 39-22 Vikings win. His start came in a 9-3 win in a monsoon over the Bears in Chicago in Week 2. Murray or Wentz in primetime this week for Minnesota? We'll have to wait and see.

home.headline: Vikings announce huge Carson Wentz decision for Week 9 vs. Bills
home.blurb: Vikings announce huge Carson Wentz decision for Week 9 vs. Bills | Sporting News Skip to main content SN 140 Watch Watch How to Watch Streaming Services fubo Add Sporting News on Google div))]:my-4" data-testid="advert--mobile_branded_logo" id="Branded_Logo_Mobile"> After their first loss of the season, the Minnesota Vikings sit at 6-1. Following their loss to the Detroit Lions , the Vikings are set to face the 6-1 Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football. As the NFL trade deadline is right around the corner, the Vikings will look to get back in the win column against one of the best teams in the NFL. It won't be easy, especially since the Vikings are making a big change. Thanks to Kyler Murray's hamstring injury, the Vikings, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter , have made the decision to start Carson Wentz on Monday Night against the Bills. Vikings to start Carson Wentz vs. Bills as Kyler Murray deals with hamstring injury "Just in: Vikings QB Carson Wentz will start Monday night's game vs. the Buffalo Bills while Kyler Murray deals with what the team has called a 'sore hamstring'," Schefter reports. Kevin O'Connell told reporters this news Thursday, the team's first day of practice leading up to Week 9 against the Bills on Monday Night Football. Facing a shaky Bills defense, the Vikings will hand the keys to the offense over to Wentz as Murray deals with this hamstring injury. It's not likely a lengthy absence for Murray, as it's only a week-to-week issue, but if Wentz impresses, the Vikings might stick with the former Philadelphia Eagles and Indianapolis Colts QB for the foreseeable future. MORE : 4 stats that show how bad Chargers' Justin Herbert has been in 2026 The Vikings got a chance to see Wentz early this season, as he went 2-0 as the starter against the Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears , albeit in some odd game scripts, coming in after Murray's Week 1 injury, and in Week 2 during a rainy, close game. But now, Wentz has a real chance to start in primetime. A strong outing, and he might convince O'Connell to stick with him as the starting QB. Murray is not going to start for Minnesota this week as he deals with a hamstring injury, but with his lackluster production so far, Wentz has a real chance to steal this starting job. He is the Week 9 starter, but there's a non-zero chance he keeps the gig going forward. home.headline: Vikings Announce Carson Wentz Decision Amid Kyler Murray Injury & Struggles
home.blurb: Wentz's numbers from his limited playing time earlier this season whilst Murray was in concussion protocol far exceed what the former first overall pick has managed to accomplish since taking back the reins. Vikings Announce Carson Wentz Decision Amid Kyler Murray Injury and Struggles Unlock the latest Heavy on Vikings news — direct to your inbox. The Minnesota Vikings have been accused of preparing a "soft benching" for struggling quarterback Kyler Murray for much of this past week as the former Arizona Cardinal deals with a hamstring injury. Having yet to announce an injury report, considering that they play on Monday night against the Buffalo Bills , head coach Kevin O'Connell had not given much concreted indication as to what Murray's practice or playing status might look like over the coming days. However, speaking to the media on Thursday, O'Connell revealed that Murray's injury will force him to miss Monday's game, and that Carson Wentz will start instead. When healthy, Wentz has thrived in Kevin O'Connell's offense. Now, a shot at 1 of the NFL's best. " The #Vikings are planning to start Carson Wentz on MNF against the #Bills , as Kyler Murray's hamstring injury would limit his mobility. Murray also could make it worse by playing." Ian Rapoport reported on Thursday. Is This a Soft Benching for Kyler Murray? The Super Bowl champion from 2018 has a passer rating 20 points higher than Murray, averages 0.44 more yards per throw, and has a far better touchdown to interception ratio (3:0 v.s. 5:3). Minnesota have a gruelling three-game schedule against the Bills, Packers and 49ers over the next three weeks, and whilst the injury may simply be a coincidence, it could also be that O'Connell knows he will need his best at the helm in order to remain contenders to top the NFC North and the conference as a whole. Brosmer is set to back up Carson Wentz against the Bills on Monday, as Kyler Murray (hamstring) won't play, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports. It would likely take an injury to Wentz for Brosmer to get into the game, but the latter moves one step closer to getting on the field for the first time in 2026. Brosmer didn't look like an NFL-caliber QB as a rookie in 2025, posting a 0:4 TD:INT across seven appearances, including two starts.
